solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Applaud actor who overdoes it in South London area

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A theatre audience cheers a hammy performer at a show in a South London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham is a district of south London, known for its Common and the 'man on the Clapham omnibus'.

clue.text: Maybe Tom from Warrington, one with a lingering happy expression

definitions.text: one with a lingering happy expression

parts.note: Warrington is a town historically in the county of Cheshire, in north-west England
a tom is a male cat, so Tom is one example of a cat

explanation.surface: A man called Tom from Warrington is remembered for his enduring smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name, but it is a tomcat. Cheshire is a county in north-west England containing Warrington.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice in Wonderland the grinning feline fades away until only its smile remains, a lingering happy expression.

clue.text: White LP, almost complete

parts.note: an LP, a long-playing record, is an album

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for complete is dropped

parts.note: to complete something is to end it

explanation.surface: A record nearly finished, perhaps a nod to the Beatles' White Album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like it belongs with 'LP' (the Beatles' White Album) but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, the clear protein that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: Firm multiplied by showing work of Dickens

parts.note: firm and hard are synonyms, as of a surface
multiplied by is said as 'times' in arithmetic

explanation.surface: A business's profits multiplied, shown in a novelist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is an 1854 novel by Charles Dickens set in an industrial town.

clue.text: Ponder extraterrestrial form of sea life

parts.note: to mull something over is to ponder it
ET is the abbreviation for extraterrestrial, as in the film

explanation.surface: Someone muses on alien life forms living in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The mullet is a fish, an example of marine life.

clue.text: Travel about, moving over

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the next word shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller wandering about while relocating.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to wander or travel about without a fixed destination.

clue.text: Prune without its skin makes you go fast!

indicators.note: without its skin means the outer letters of the fruit's name are peeled off

explanation.surface: A joke that prunes make you hurry, a nod to their laxative effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without its skin' strips the first and last letters off PRUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Running is moving fast on foot; the verb sense of hurrying fits 'go fast'.

clue.text: Safe place to jump

definitions.meaning: a strongroom in a bank where valuables are kept secure
to leap over something, using hands or a pole

explanation.surface: A secure spot from which to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank's strongroom is a vault, and vaulting is leaping over an obstacle, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Remnant of fire found at the end of three months

definitions.meaning: a glowing piece of coal or wood left after a fire

definitions.text: found at the end of three months
definitions.meaning: September, November and December all close with the same five letters

explanation.surface: Something left from a fire discovered at the end of a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal left after a fire dies down is an ember; the second definition is the shared ending of three month names.

clue.text: Listless, glad Uni is out

indicators.note: is out suggests the letters are disordered or put out of place

explanation.surface: A tired student is pleased the university term has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid and listless both describe someone lacking energy or enthusiasm, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Part of meal being cooked perhaps with unusual style, not in the true way?

parts.note: a dish is one course or part of a meal
food being cooked is 'on' the stove

indicators.note: unusual signals an arrangement of the letters of style that is out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a course in an odd style that strays from tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STYLE into ESTLY. The question mark flags a definition by roundabout description.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without honesty means behaving untruthfully, so 'not in the true way' describes the adverb.

clue.text: The man that can be heard in church song

indicators.note: that can be heard says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a hymn is a song sung in church

explanation.surface: A man whose voice carries in a church choir.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to a male person as object, so 'the man' stands for it.

clue.text: Having written a will protecting husband and son in America

indicators.note: protecting says one word wraps round and guards the letter for husband

parts.note: testate describes someone who has made a valid will
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A man makes a will that protects his husband and son in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts H inside TESTATE after its first letter, giving THESTATE; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is an informal name for the United States, the country commonly called America.

clue.text: Part of deck on which 45 may go for a spin

definitions.text: Part of deck on which 45 may go for a spin

parts.words: Part of deck on which 45 may go for a spin
parts.note: a 45 is a single record played at 45 rpm, and a record deck has a rotating platter

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sailor on a ship's deck taking forty-five people for a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship, but it is a record player; '45' is a seven-inch single.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating platter of a record player is where vinyl spins under the stylus.

clue.text: Change designation of item, an error partly reversed

indicators.note: reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone relabels a product after spotting a mistake in its listing.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a thing a new name is to alter its designation, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Piano music's silence, with nothing played fast

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a rest is a notated silence in music
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pianist's piece has a pause, then nothing but rapid playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking meaning very quickly, a direction to the performer.

clue.text: Attendant almost to tread on person in care

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the word for tread is lost

parts.note: to step on is to tread on
a ward is a minor under the care of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: A carer nearly treads on someone they are looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant serving passengers on a ship or plane.

clue.text: To change sides is a fault

definitions.meaning: to desert one's side for the enemy, a verb
a flaw or imperfection, a noun

explanation.surface: Switching allegiance is a failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter abandons their side, and a flaw in goods is the same word as a noun, stressed differently.

clue.text: Frightfully damp reaction?

parts.note: 'Frightfully' means both 'very' and 'out of fright': a fearful response that leaves you perspiring

explanation.surface: Someone reacting to awfully wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' reads as the old-fashioned 'very', but here it means caused by fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear or anxiety makes the skin clammy with perspiration, a damp response to fright.

clue.text: Seal swimming at end of beach shows restraint for an animal

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about freely into a new order
at end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A seal swimming off the shore by a beach shows self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is held by a lead or strap, a restraint attached to its collar.

clue.text: Odd pieces removed from very new organ

indicators.note: with the first, third, fifth and seventh letters dropped, only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: Bits taken out of a brand-new organ, as in a transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the body's organ of sight.

clue.text: Edges of travelator, enough to walk on

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: ample means enough or plenty

explanation.surface: A moving walkway at an airport has plenty of room to stride along.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread heavily on something, crushing it underfoot, is to walk on it.

clue.text: Clumsily handle father and wife

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly deals with their parents.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something or someone awkwardly or with groping hands is to maul or touch clumsily.

clue.text: Proudly claim vessel carries spades

indicators.note: carries says the word for vessel holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Someone brags that their ship holds a cargo of digging tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to speak proudly of one's achievements, a synonym.

clue.text: Work with teeth, clubs and axe

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: A caveman labours with teeth, clubs and an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding food with the teeth is what eating with the molars does, a plain description.

clue.text: A study developed around English calendar item

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
developed suggests the letters of the phrase grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A piece of research grows into an English calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges ASTUDY into TUSDAY; 'around' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is one of the dated entries marked on a calendar.
